core_obligations: Reduce etale locally on Y to Y = Spec(A) affine, keeping quasi-compactness of X (proof line 329-330).

Choose an affine U = Spec(B) with a surjective etale morphism U -> X and identify U x_X U = Spec(B tensor_A B), hence the category of quasi-coherent O_X-modules with the descent category DD_{B/A} (proof lines 330-340).
Show that A -> B is universally injective by testing on A-modules: the hypothesis makes A + M -> B tensor_A (A + M) injective for every M, which is the stated criterion (proof lines 341-347).
Apply descent to get DD_{B/A} equivalent to A-modules, so that pullback along f is exact on quasi-coherent modules and f is flat, and observe that f is surjective (proof lines 349-354).
Since {X -> Spec(A)} is then an fpqc cover and X -> Spec(A) becomes an isomorphism after base change by itself, conclude by fpqc descent that f is an isomorphism (proof lines 355-359).
proof_roadmap: Etale-local reduction to an affine base and choice of an affine etale cover U = Spec(B) (proof lines 329-333).
Translate quasi-coherent sheaves on X into descent data DD_{B/A} and prove A -> B universally injective from the hypothesis (proof lines 334-347).
Use descent to obtain flatness and surjectivity of f, then apply fpqc descent of isomorphisms to the self-base-change cover (proof lines 348-359).
difficulty_reason: The lemma concerns a quasi-compact monomorphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces such that for every T -> Y the map O_T -> f_{T,*}O_{X x_Y T} is injective, and concludes that f is an isomorphism (statement lines 318-326). The proof turns the hypothesis into universal injectivity of the ring map A -> B of an affine etale presentation, translates quasi-coherent sheaves on X into descent data DD_{B/A}, and then uses descent to compute that f^* is exact on quasi-coherent modules (proof lines 334-352). The non-routine step is precisely that translation: the injectivity hypothesis is used on the split module A + M to produce the universal injectivity that the descent theorem needs, after which flatness and surjectivity of f and the fpqc descent of isomorphism finish the proof (proof lines 341-359). The author flags one small omission, the passage to flatness (proof line 353), so H2.
